cases.q1: SELECT region FROM orders
cases.q2: SELECT DISTINCT region FROM orders
cases.note: set-equal; the plain query repeats rows the DISTINCT one collapses

cases.q1: SELECT DISTINCT region FROM orders
cases.q2: SELECT region FROM orders
cases.note: DISTINCT only removes duplicates

cases.q1: SELECT DISTINCT region FROM orders WHERE amount > 10
cases.q2: SELECT region FROM orders
cases.note: a filtered DISTINCT is still within the plain rows

cases.q1: SELECT region FROM orders WHERE amount > 10
cases.q2: SELECT DISTINCT region FROM orders
cases.note: set-contained; bag-wise the filtered rows can repeat

cases.q1: SELECT DISTINCT region FROM orders
cases.q2: SELECT DISTINCT region FROM orders WHERE amount > 10

cases.q1: SELECT DISTINCT status FROM orders
cases.q2: SELECT DISTINCT status FROM orders WHERE region = 1

cases.q2: SELECT DISTINCT id FROM orders

cases.q1: SELECT DISTINCT id FROM orders WHERE amount > 5
cases.q2: SELECT id FROM orders
cases.note: id is a key

cases.q1: SELECT status, region FROM orders
cases.q2: SELECT region, status FROM orders
cases.note: same columns in a different order are different rows

cases.q2: SELECT id, amount + 1 FROM orders WHERE amount > 5
cases.note: same projection, weaker filter on the right

cases.q1: SELECT id, amount + 1 FROM orders WHERE amount > 10
cases.q2: SELECT id, amount FROM orders WHERE amount > 5
cases.note: different second column

cases.q1: SELECT id, 1 FROM orders WHERE amount > 10
cases.q2: SELECT id, 1 FROM orders
cases.note: constant column unchanged

cases.q1: SELECT id, region FROM orders WHERE region = 3

cases.q1: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE amount > 10

cases.q2: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE amount > 10

cases.q1: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE amount > 10 UNION SELECT id FROM orders WHERE amount > 10
cases.q2: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE amount > 10 UNION ALL SELECT id FROM orders WHERE amount > 10

cases.q1: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE amount > 10 UNION ALL SELECT id FROM orders WHERE amount > 10
cases.q2: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE amount > 10 UNION SELECT id FROM orders WHERE amount > 10

cases.q1: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE amount > 10 EXCEPT SELECT id FROM orders WHERE region = 1

cases.q2: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE region = 1

cases.q1: SELECT o.id FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id

cases.note: customers.id is a key, so the join cannot duplicate an order

cases.q1: SELECT id FROM orders
cases.q2: SELECT o.id FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
cases.note: orders without a customer are lost by the join

cases.q1: SELECT o.id FROM orders o JOIN events e ON o.customer_id = e.customer_id
cases.q2: SELECT id FROM orders
cases.note: events has no key, so a matching order repeats once per event

cases.q1: SELECT DISTINCT o.id FROM orders o JOIN events e ON o.customer_id = e.customer_id
cases.q2: SELECT id FROM orders
cases.note: DISTINCT removes the join's repeats

cases.q1: SELECT o.id, c.tier FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
cases.q2: SELECT o.id, c.tier FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
cases.note: same join written the other way round

cases.q1: SELECT o.id FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE c.tier = 1
cases.q2: SELECT o.id FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
cases.note: filter on the joined table

cases.q1: SELECT o.id FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
cases.q2: SELECT o.id FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE c.tier = 1
cases.note: the unfiltered join has other tiers

cases.q1: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT id FROM customers WHERE tier = 1)
cases.q2: SELECT o.id FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
cases.note: customers.id is a key, so IN and JOIN return the same rows; the filter only narrows

cases.q1: SELECT o.id, c.tier FROM orders o LEFT JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
cases.q2: SELECT o.id, c.tier FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id

cases.q1: SELECT o.id, c.tier FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
cases.q2: SELECT o.id, c.tier FROM orders o LEFT JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
cases.note: an inner join is a subset of the left join

cases.q1: SELECT a.id FROM orders a JOIN orders b ON a.id = b.id
cases.q2: SELECT id FROM orders
cases.note: self-join on a key returns each row once

cases.q1: SELECT o.id FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.region = c.region
cases.q2: SELECT id FROM orders
cases.note: region is not a key of customers: matches can repeat

cases.q1: SELECT region, COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE amount > 10 GROUP BY region
cases.q2: SELECT region, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY region

cases.q1: SELECT region, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY region
cases.q2: SELECT region, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY region HAVING COUNT(*) > 2

cases.q2: SELECT region, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY region HAVING COUNT(*) > 2

cases.q2: SELECT region, COUNT(amount) FROM orders GROUP BY region
